title: Bilal, "One, One"
hookLine: Umayyah lays a rock on Bilal in the sun, and he says only ahad

cards: Abu Talib could shield his nephew. Not everyone who believed had an uncle like that. Some had no clan to stand behind them at all.
Some were owned. Midday in the open valley of Mecca, the hottest hour. The ground burns.
A man lies on his back on it, held there by a heavy stone on his chest, while the man who owns him stands over him, waiting for him to give in. Today: Bilal.

teach.b: Bilal ibn Rabah was enslaved in Mecca, the property of Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and he had come to believe. Ibn Ishaq tells what Umayyah did.

teach.h: THE ROCK IN THE MIDDAY SUN.
teach.b: He would bring Bilal out in the heat of the day, throw him on his back in the open valley, and have a great rock laid on his chest.
Then he would tell him: you will stay like this until you die, or until you deny Muhammad and worship the idols of Quraysh. And Bilal, under the stone, would say one word.
One. He didn't argue or make a speech; he had almost no breath to make one with. One word carried his whole answer to the idols: one God, not many.
It is the same word that closes the first verse of a short surah of the Qur'an, which Pickthall translates: "Say: He is Allah, the One!"

The sirah goes on: Abu Bakr passed by while this was happening, and he bought Bilal from Umayyah and set him free. Yesterday a clan head shielded the Prophet. Today a friend uses his wealth to shield a slave.

teach.h: SAY: HE IS ALLAH, THE ONE!
teach.b: Later in the story, al-Bukhari's reports name Bilal as the one who gave the call to prayer, the voice that called the believers in Medina.
The man who could only manage one word under a stone became the voice that called them to prayer. That is for later. Today, there is only the heat, the stone, and the word.

how: Muslims honor Bilal as an early companion and remember his 'ahad, ahad' in sermons and sirah study; the one who gives the call to prayer, the role he held, is called the mu'adhdhin.

games.q: you're under a stone in the midday sun. you're told to deny your faith or stay there. you have almost no breath. what do you say?
o: whatever they want, to end it.
games.why: Ibn Ishaq says Bilal said only ahad, ahad. one, one. then Abu Bakr bought and freed him.

practice: Choose one word that holds what you most trust: for Bilal it was ahad, and if you're Muslim you might choose it too; if not, choose your own, a name, a value, a promise.
Breathe in, and on the out-breath say it, softly or silently; when the mind wanders, come back to the one word.

wordCard.voice: Bilal. The enslaved believer who, under a rock in the midday sun, said only ahad, one, until Abu Bakr bought his freedom. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: one, the One; the word Bilal repeated, and the word in surah 112:1.

carryVoice: Your line: ahad. One word can hold a whole answer. Day seven hundred thirty-six, done.
